claims.text: Key takeaway: first confirm you owe the bill, check charges, then dispute anything wrong
claims.quote: If you can't pay a medical bill, first make sure you owe the amount charged. Review the bill for errors, check that your health insurance was applied correctly

claims.text: Key takeaway: surprise-bill protections and financial assistance (charity care) can reduce what you owe or provide free or discounted care
claims.quote: You may also have protections under federal or state law that reduce what you owe ... Financial assistance programs, sometimes called “charity care,” provide free or discounted health care

claims.text: Key takeaway: negotiate and ask about an interest-free repayment plan before using a credit card
claims.quote: Negotiate the bill down to an amount that you can afford; Ask if the provider will accept an interest-free repayment plan ... Be careful about using a credit card or a medical credit card to pay off the bill.

claims.text: Step one: confirm you have not already paid and have not been confused with someone with a similar name
claims.quote: First, make sure that you owe the bill. You could have already paid it. It’s also possible that the provider or debt collector has confused you with someone else with a similar name.

claims.text: Step two: ask for an itemized list, look for errors such as duplicate charges, check insurance was applied correctly
claims.quote: ask for an itemized list of charges ... Look for billing errors like being charged for the same service or treatment twice.

claims.text: Step two: contact the billing office promptly to avoid late fees and interest
claims.quote: talk to the accounting or billing office of your provider ... You want to do this quickly so you can get any charges resolved and to avoid late fees and interest.

claims.text: Step three: right to internal appeal and external review; can dispute with debt collector or credit reporting company
claims.quote: You have a right to both an “ internal appeal” and an “ external review” of the charges. ... you can also dispute a medical bill with a debt collector or a credit reporting company.

claims.text: Step four: some services such as ground ambulance are not protected by the No Surprises Act
claims.quote: Some services, such as ground ambulance transportation services, are NOT protected by the No Surprises Act.

claims.text: Step five: ACA requires 501(c)(3) nonprofit hospitals to have financial assistance (charity care) programs providing free or discounted care
claims.quote: Financial assistance programs, sometimes called “charity care,” provide free or discounted health care to people who need help paying their medical bills. The Affordable Care Act (ACA) requires hospitals with 501(c)(3) nonprofit status to have programs to provide this care

claims.text: Step six: ask to reduce the bill to an affordable amount or accept an interest-free repayment plan
claims.quote: Negotiate the bill down to an amount that you can afford; Ask if the provider will accept an interest-free repayment plan

claims.text: Credit card or medical credit card may carry high interest and you may lose the ability to negotiate
claims.quote: Be careful about using a credit card or a medical credit card to pay off the bill. There may be high interest and you may lose the ability to negotiate the debt.

claims.text: State consumer assistance programs help with health insurance problems; state AG or insurance department/commissioner may offer information and a complaint process
claims.quote: Many states provide help for consumers experiencing problems with their health insurance. ... State agencies such as your state attorney general and state insurance department or insurance commissioner may also offer helpful information as well as a complaint process.

claims.text: CFPB complaint for debt-collection or credit-reporting problems tied to a surprise medical bill
claims.quote: If you have a problem with debt collection because of a surprise medical bill, or a problem with credit reporting because of surprise medical charges ... you can submit a complaint with the CFPB online

claims.text: Call script note: CFPB suggests asking for both a reduction and a payment plan
claims.quote: Negotiate the bill down to an amount that you can afford; Ask if the provider will accept an interest-free repayment plan

claims.text: Doing nothing can lead to late fees and interest, debt collection, lawsuits, garnishments, and lower credit scores (body and FAQ)
claims.quote: If you do nothing and don’t pay, you could be facing late fees and interest, debt collection, lawsuits, garnishments, and lower credit scores.

claims.text: FAQ negotiate: lower the bill, interest-free repayment plan, be careful with credit cards
claims.quote: Negotiate the bill down to an amount that you can afford; Ask if the provider will accept an interest-free repayment plan; ... Be careful about using a credit card or a medical credit card

claims.text: FAQ dispute: itemized list, compare with EOB, raise with billing office; appeal rights with insurer
claims.quote: ask for an itemized list of charges ... talk to the accounting or billing office of your provider ... You have a right to both an “ internal appeal” and an “ external review” of the charges.

claims.text: FAQ credit card: high interest, lose ability to negotiate, interest-free repayment plan may be better
claims.quote: There may be high interest and you may lose the ability to negotiate the debt. There may be better options like an interest-free repayment plan.

claims.text: FAQ first thing: confirm you owe it and check charges against the EOB
claims.quote: first make sure you owe the amount charged. Review the bill for errors, check that your health insurance was applied correctly ... Check your health insurance policy documents and the “explanation of benefits.”

claims.text: Key takeaway and perspective: medical debt is a low priority behind more pressing debts such as mortgage, rent, or car loan
claims.quote: treat medical debt as a low priority debt to be paid only after you pay more pressing types of debt, such as your mortgage, car loan ... ahead of more important bills, such as your rent or home mortgage.

claims.text: Do not put medical debt on a credit card, even a medical credit card, unless you can pay the card and all other obligations that month
claims.quote: Also don’t put medical debt on your credit card, even a “medical” credit card, unless you can pay the card and all your other obligations that month.

claims.text: Step two: compare the bill with your explanation of benefits
claims.quote: Also review any explanation of benefits (EOB) form you receive from your insurance company to see if it is consistent with the medical bill.

claims.text: Charging the bill to a card loses the option to negotiate with the provider because it becomes credit card debt
claims.quote: You lose the option of negotiating with your health care provider over the bill. Using this type of card turns your medical debt into credit card debt.

claims.text: Low priority does not mean ignoring the bill
claims.quote: Medical debt’s status as a low priority debt does not mean that one should ignore medical debt.

claims.text: Applies to coverage through an employer, the Marketplace, or an individual plan; bans surprise bills for most emergency services
claims.quote: If you get health coverage through your employer, a Health Insurance Marketplace, or an individual health insurance plan ... these new rules will: Ban surprise bills for most emergency services

claims.text: Limits you to in-network cost-sharing for most emergency and some non-emergency services
claims.quote: Ban out-of-network cost-sharing (like out-of-network coinsurance or copayments) for most emergency and some non-emergency services. You can’t be charged more than in-network cost-sharing for these services.

claims.text: Bans balance bills for certain services such as anesthesiology or radiology from out-of-network providers during a visit to an in-network facility
claims.quote: Ban out-of-network charges and balance bills for certain additional services (like anesthesiology or radiology) furnished by out-of-network providers as part of a patient’s visit to an in-network facility.

claims.text: A nonprofit hospital must decide on a complete application submitted during the 240-day application period starting with the first post-discharge bill
claims.quote: a 240-day “application period,” ... beginning on the date the first “post-discharge” billing statement is provided. ... who submits a complete FAP application during the 240-day application period, the hospital facility determines whether the individual is FAP-eligible

claims.text: A hospital may accept applications at any time
claims.quote: A hospital facility may continue to accept and process FAP applications from patients at any time.

claims.text: Denying, delaying, or requiring payment before medically necessary care because of unpaid past bills is an extraordinary collection action
claims.quote: involve deferring or denying, or requiring a payment before providing, medically necessary care because of an individual’s non-payment of one or more bills for previously provided care covered under the hospital facility’s FAP

claims.text: ECAs only after reasonable efforts, including notifying about the FAP and waiting at least 120 days after the first post-discharge bill
claims.quote: notifies the individual about the FAP before initiating any ECAs to obtain payment for the care and refrains from initiating such ECAs for at least 120 days from the date the hospital facility provides the first post-discharge billing statement

claims.text: Applying for financial assistance may reduce or clear the debt
claims.quote: If an individual qualifies for free care, the hospital facility must provide them with a written notification that nothing more is owed. ... qualifies for less than free care ... billing statement that indicates the amount the individual owes

claims.text: Debt collector must give validation information, including the end date of the validation period
claims.quote: a debt collector must provide a consumer with the validation information required by paragraph (c) of this section ... The date that the debt collector will consider the end date of the validation period

claims.text: Validation period runs until 30 days after the consumer receives the validation information
claims.quote: Validation period means the period starting on the date that a debt collector provides the validation information ... and ending 30 days after the consumer receives or is assumed to receive the validation information.

claims.text: A written dispute by that date requires the collector to stop collecting the disputed amount until it sends verification or a copy of a judgment
claims.quote: if the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing on or before that date ... the debt collector must cease collection ... until the debt collector sends ... verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment.

claims.text: FAQ: if a debt collector has the account, dispute in writing before the validation period ends
claims.quote: if the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing on or before that date that the debt, or any portion of the debt, is disputed, the debt collector must cease collection of the debt

claims.text: Paid medical collection debt left off reports since July 1, 2022; unpaid medical collection debt does not appear until one year
claims.quote: Effective July 1, 2022, paid medical collection debt is no longer included on U.S. consumer credit reports. In addition, the time period before unpaid medical collection debt appears on a consumer’s report was increased from 6 months to one year

claims.text: Since April 2023, medical collection debt with an initial balance under $500 is left off
claims.quote: removed medical collection debt with an initial reported balance of under $500 from U.S. consumer credit reports as of April 2023.
